Actual Article Body:
By Jen Rice

September 1, 2026

Republican officials in a key battleground Texas county are set to vote Tuesday on a revised plan that would cut Election Day polling locations by 30% for the November midterm elections.

The new proposal they will vote on Tuesday calls for 224 Election Day locations, down from 316 in the 2022 midterms. It also includes 47 early voting locations, down from 50.

Tarrant County commissioners initially considered a plan at their Aug. 4 meeting that would have slashed almost half of the Election Day voting locations and closed eight early voting sites, including some on college campuses. But the GOP officials postponed the final vote to September in the face of considerable outrage from voters.
